card.occupation: Between jobs. Until this spring she was an office coordinator at a residential property management company in Stratford. The firm restructured and her role was merged, and she took voluntary redundancy. She is now applying for operations and office manager roles and doing a short online bookkeeping course.
card.education_detail: Went to secondary school and sixth form in Enfield (A-levels in Business, Sociology and Maths). Completed a BA in Business Management at Middlesex University while working part-time in retail. She is currently partway through an AAT Level 2 bookkeeping certificate, studying online.
card.household: Rents a one-bedroom flat above a row of shops near Hoe Street with her partner Callum (30), a sound technician who works on theatre and corporate events. They have been together five years and living together for three. No children and no pets, though they keep discussing getting a cat. Her parents and younger brother live in Enfield, about forty minutes away on the bus, and she sees them most weekends.
card.cultural_background: Born in Prizren, Kosovo. She moved to London aged nine with her mum, dad and baby brother after her dad got work through a cousin already here. She grew up speaking Albanian at home and English everywhere else, and now uses English more than Albanian, apart from on the phone to her nan. Her family are Muslim in the relaxed Kosovar way. She doesn't drink much, fasts for some of Ramadan with her mum, and goes to the mosque for Eid. She calls her faith 'more about family and how you treat people than rules.' Her parents took a while to come round to her living with Callum before marriage. Things are fine now and her mum feeds him constantly.
card.professional_persona: The person in an office who knows where everything is and who to ask. She is good at keeping contractors, tenants and managers all on the same page without anyone losing their temper. She is reliable and well prepared, and quietly proud of the spreadsheets and handover documents she left behind. In meetings she is friendly and chatty, but she won't oversell herself. She finds 'tell me about your strengths' interview questions genuinely awkward.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive sense. She goes to a local gym three mornings a week, mostly for spin classes because she likes the group energy and the instructor shouting. She walks a lot round Lloyd Park and along the Lea. She half-follows Arsenal because her dad and brother do and watches the big matches at her parents' house.
card.arts_persona: Callum gets free or cheap theatre tickets through work, so she sees more shows than she otherwise would. She likes musicals and anything funny, and finds heavy drama a bit much. She listens to pop and Albanian wedding music, the latter partly ironically. She watches Love Island and The Traitors with friends over group chat and reads a couple of thrillers a year on holiday.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Kosovo most summers for two or three weeks to see grandparents and cousins. These trips are less a holiday than a run of family visits. She has done a couple of city breaks with Callum (Lisbon, Porto) and a girls' trip to Tenerife. She plans everything in advance with a shared note listing flight times and restaurant ideas.
card.culinary_persona: A good home cook who learned from her mum. She makes flija for special occasions (badly, she claims), and pite, stuffed peppers and big trays of roast veg. Day to day it's quick pasta or stir-fry for dinner. Callum does the Sunday roast. They avoid pork at home mainly out of habit and respect for her family rather than strict observance. She loves a Turkish place on the high street and gets excited about good baklava.
hobbies_and_interests: Spin classes and long walks around Walthamstow Wetlands
Cooking family recipes and trying to write them down properly
Going to theatre and comedy nights with Callum
Reality TV with a group chat running commentary
Charity shop and Vinted browsing for clothes
Volunteering occasionally at a local food bank since leaving work
skills: Scheduling and coordinating lots of people and moving parts
Excel and Google Sheets, building trackers and simple formulas
Calm, polite handling of annoyed customers on the phone
Bilingual in English and Albanian (spoken better than written)
Organising family events and keeping everyone in the loop
card.career_goals: Wants a stable office or operations manager role, ideally at a smaller company where she isn't 'just a number', within the next few months. Longer term she'd like to move into finance or operations properly once she finishes her AAT qualifications. She wants enough security that she and Callum can think about saving for a deposit, and eventually about marriage and kids.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty. She speaks a natural London English with no foreign accent, slightly softer when she's being polite. She talks fairly fast when she's interested and laughs easily, including at herself. She uses 'erm' when thinking, 'sort of' and 'kind of' as hedges, and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah'. She drops in an occasional 'innit' with friends but rarely on a formal call. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'my mum'. She apologises a lot, and 'sorry' doubles as a repair word ('sorry, I mean the second one'). She tends to echo the question back before answering ('what do I do on weekends? Erm, mostly...'). She finds silence slightly uncomfortable and will fill it, or ask 'does that make sense?'
card.typing: Mostly correct and tidy because she's used to work emails. She capitalises the start of sentences and names, uses apostrophes properly, and sometimes skips the final full stop. She occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'idk' in very quick answers, but not usually in a form. Answers are short but complete, sometimes with a second sentence of explanation tacked on.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and open almost immediately. She asks questions back, makes small jokes and is easy to talk to. Underneath she is a bit of a worrier: she wants to give the 'right' answer and will double-check what's being asked. She is honest even when it doesn't flatter her, and is quick to downplay her own achievements.
small_things: Callum coming home at midnight after a get-out at the theatre
Trying to perfect her mum's pite recipe
Hoe Street being dug up for the third time this year
The neighbour's cat that sits on their windowsill
Being knackered after a day of job applications that somehow feels harder than work
deeper_things: Feeling a bit lost and embarrassed about not working, even though the redundancy wasn't her fault
Worrying about money and whether they'll ever be able to buy anywhere in London
The tension with her parents when she first moved in with Callum, and how much it upset her
Remembering arriving in London at nine with no English and being terrified at school
Her grandparents getting older in Kosovo and guilt about not being there more
Not being sure where her faith sits for her, and not wanting to disappoint her mum
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot at a slightly low angle, framed from mid-chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Daylight comes from a window out of frame on the right, so the right side of her face is brighter, and there is a faint blue glow from the screen. She has an oval face, light olive skin and dark brown eyes. She smiles politely with her lips closed, eyebrows slightly raised as if mid-listening. Dark brown shoulder-length hair is pulled back into a loose low ponytail, with a few strands loose at the front. She wears small gold hoop earrings and a thin gold chain, and no glasses. She is in a plain grey crewneck sweatshirt. Behind her is a cream-painted wall with a framed print of a lemon tree. Below it is the top of a mustard-coloured sofa with a folded knitted throw on the arm. To the left is a tall leafy plant in a white pot and part of a wall-mounted shelf holding a few paperbacks, a candle and a small framed photo too small to make out.
